VERDICT: the approved contract changes no signature, so this stage has nothing to write. Evidence below, then the three things the next stages need from me.

== 1. The contract names no C# surface ==

`Surfaces` (contract lines 73-85) lists `ts/metalang/render.ts`, `app.tsx`, `client.tsx`, `arch.yaml`, `metalang.yaml`, `kit.ts`, `kit-entry.ts`, the three test files, `guardrails.test.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `bunfig.toml`, `.agents/workflows/*.js`, and `rails-test-code`/`rails-run-a-workflow` SKILL.md. No path under `src/`, `tests/` or `analyzers/` appears anywhere in the contract. Every `What to do` item lands in `ts/`, `.github/` or `.agents/`.

== 2. The one unbuilt decision changes no signature ==

Unbuilt: `member-identity-unique` (contract line 29) — "A name that occurs more than once gives each of those rows an identity written as that name, a number sign, and the row's place among the members of that declaration carrying that same name, counting from one in the order the source declares them — `PrecheckAsync#1` and `PrecheckAsync#2` ... and no row carries the shared name on its own."

Live state, read from the working tree: `/Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/ts/metalang/app.tsx:747-754` returns the bare name — `const named = text(held); return named.length === 0 ? undefined : named`. No `#` anywhere in `ts/metalang/*.ts{,x}` production or test source.

Why no signature: `identityOf` is a local arrow inside the module-local `Table` component (app.tsx:724-754). It is not exported, is in no interface, and no test can reach it. The `members: readonly Mapping[]` it needs to count occurrences is already its enclosing props. The contract also forbids giving it a new named owner — `Reuse ledger` line 1: "reuse `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` at `ts/metalang/words.ts:422`, called once per table beside the existing `columns` computation ... Write no second resolver, no fallback chain and no type-derivation route beside it." Declaring a new exported identity helper would be shape the contract did not decide and a Reuse-ledger violation, so I declared none.

== 3. Everything else the contract decides is already built, and I stubbed none of it ==

Per `rails-run-a-workflow`: "ARCHITECTURE never stubs unchanged working code back to a throw." Verified present and left byte-identical: `role: name` on `member.name` plus the widened role meaning (commit cfbbbf5); `data-declaration` at app.tsx:1508 through the one extracted predicate `idOf` at app.tsx:1739; `data-member` at app.tsx:780 through `propertyCarrying` at app.tsx:745; the helper tag at render.ts:62 (`STORY_SCRIPT`), :80 (`STORY_HELPER`) and :96 (its position in the shell); `NotNarratedHere` at app.tsx:1724 with client.tsx reading `window.__jarvisStory` after `DOMContentLoaded`; the kit readme sentence at kit.ts:109-110; jsdom 31.0.0 and `@types/jsdom` 30.0.0 in package.json/bun.lock; `style.css`/`syntax.css` in ci.yml; and the `impact-test` rewrite already in guardrails.test.ts:1364-1385. Working tree is clean (`git status --short` empty) and was clean before and after my run.

== What TDD needs, and why it can go RED without me ==

Acceptance 18 ("Command: `bun test ts/metalang/app.test.tsx`") is written against the DOM of the rendered component, so it compiles against the existing exported surface: `Page`, `Declaration`, `idOf`, `text`, `kindStyle` from app.tsx, the test file's own fixture builders `archDocument` (app.test.tsx:70), `archMember` (:1745), `archElement` (:1754), and `JSDOM` already imported at app.test.tsx:12. `What the agent MAY do` already authorizes "test fixtures that declare shapes carrying punctuation, quotes and repeated member names". RED is the expanded-behavior kind the rails define: "expanded behavior is RED through an expected-versus-actual failure against the required behavior" — a fixture with two `PrecheckAsync` members will draw two rows both carrying `data-member="PrecheckAsync"`, so the `#1`/`#2` assertions fail and the "shared name alone matches none" assertion fails. Nothing must exist for those tests to be written that does not exist now.

== Fence ==

No rule was approved to remain a warning: contract line 41 — "None of the three is an analyzer and none carries a diagnostic id, so no diagnostic is approved to remain a warning in any intermediate build." `ruleWarningIds` was None, so I ran the plain `dotnet build -c Release`: 0 warnings, 0 errors, exit 0. Writing no file, I could not breach the fence, and I suppressed, `NoWarn`-ed, lowered or edited nothing.

== One thing the orchestrator should know ==

This stage's PROVE command builds C#, while every line of code this contract changes is TypeScript. The handed command is green, and I additionally ran the TypeScript compile (`bun run typecheck`, exit 0) so the claim "the surface TDD compiles against is clean" rests on the compiler that actually governs it. I did not treat the typecheck as a substitute for the required build. Nothing here is a decision; I am flagging it so the panel and the human read the proof for what it is.

No wall. I wrote no test, no behavior, and no file. The independent SOLID/DRY/Lie-catcher panel is still required on this contract-backed no-signature result.
